answer.policy_title: CMM-311: Knee Replacement/Arthroplasty (Comprehensive Musculoskeletal Management Guidelines) — developed by EviCore healthcare and used by Cigna to make medical necessity determinations for knee replacement/arthroplasty CPT codes, including 27446
answer.effective_date: Version 2.0.2025, Effective November 5, 2025 (published/updated August 12, 2025). This is the version that appears to have been in force on the August 1, 2026 notice date — note a newer Version 1.0.2026 (Effective August 4, 2026) was published just three days after this notice, so it is possible (though I could not confirm from the denial letter itself) that the reviewer used either the 2025 or the about-to-take-effect 2026 version. Both versions I retrieved contain essentially identical partial-knee-replacement criteria.
criteria_quotes: Partial knee replacement (medial, lateral, or patellofemoral) is considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria have been met:

Imaging or arthroscopic findings show EITHER of the following: — severe unicompartmental (medial, lateral, or patellofemoral) osteoarthritis as evidenced by ANY of the following: Kellgren-Lawrence Grade IV radiographic findings; Outerbridge Classification Grade IV arthroscopic findings AND not a candidate for joint sparing procedure; Modified Outerbridge Classification Grade IV MRI findings AND not a candidate for joint sparing procedure — OR unicompartmental avascular necrosis (AVN) of the femoral condyles and/or proximal tibia
Physical exam demonstrates BOTH of the following findings: knee stability; knee arc of motion (full extension to full flexion) >90º

Symptoms include BOTH of the following: function-limiting pain at short distances (e.g., walking less than one-quarter mile, limiting activity to two city blocks, the equivalent to walking the length of a shopping mall) for at least three (3) months duration; loss of knee function which interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment

Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months duration. Criteria exception: Provider-directed non-surgical management may be inappropriate. The medical record must clearly document why provider-directed non-surgical management is not appropriate.
Note: It is incumbent on the surgeon to preoperatively optimize reasonably modifiable medical and behavioral health comorbidities.
answer.appeal_deadline: The denial letter itself states the appeal must be received within 180 days of the notice date (2026-08-01), i.e., by 2027-01-28. Note: Cigna's general Arizona Health Care Insurer Appeals Process Information Packet separately states members generally 'have two years from the date of an Adverse Determination to begin the health care appeals process' for Arizona-regulated plans — this is a longer window than the letter's 180-day language. Because the two documents conflict, the patient should treat the 180-day deadline stated in the actual denial letter as controlling and file well before 2027-01-28 to be safe, while also asking Cigna in writing to confirm which deadline applies to this specific plan.
answer.submission_route: Per Cigna's standard 'Customer Appeal Request' process: (1) First call Cigna Customer Service at the number on the back of the member ID card to see if the issue can be resolved informally. (2) If not resolved, mail a completed Customer Appeal Request form and/or an appeal letter (marked 'Customer Appeal' if no form is used) plus supporting documentation (copy of this denial letter, and — critically — medical records/imaging and a physician statement addressing the CMM-311 criteria above) to the appeal address indicated by the member's ID card type. Cigna's form lists these addresses: for 'Cigna Network' ID cards — Cigna Appeals Unit, P.O. Box 188062, Chattanooga, TN 37422-8062; for 'GW - Cigna' or 'G' on the front — Cigna Appeals Unit, P.O. Box 188011, Chattanooga, TN 37422-8011; for 'Cigna-HealthSpring' (Medicare) — AZ Medicare Appeals Unit, 25500 N Norterra Dr., Bldg. B, Phoenix, AZ 85085-8200 (not applicable here since this is a commercial/ACA plan). Because the correct P.O. Box depends on the exact wording on Reese's ID card, the patient should confirm the address printed on the ID card or in the denial letter itself before mailing. Arizona also permits filing by phone, and after an internal denial the member may pursue an External Independent Review through the Arizona Department of Insurance and Financial Institutions (AZ DIFI).
answer.how_to_obtain_criteria: The full CMM-311 guideline (including the exact indications/non-indications language quoted above) is publicly posted by EviCore, which develops these guidelines for Cigna. In addition, the patient/provider has a right to request the specific clinical review criteria actually used to make this determination directly from Cigna by calling the number on the ID card or the denial letter and citing reference number POC-8AD74FF769-66861; Cigna is required to provide the medical necessity criteria applied to this specific denial upon request, and this should be requested in writing as part of the appeal.
answer.notes: I was able to retrieve full text of the EviCore-authored CMM-311 'Partial Knee Replacement Indications' criteria from three versions (effective July 2025, November 2025, and August 2026) — the substantive medical-necessity criteria for partial knee replacement are essentially unchanged across these versions. However, I could not confirm from any document I retrieved (i) which exact version number Cigna's reviewer cited for this specific determination, or (ii) whether this particular Arizona commercial/ACA plan delegates PA review for CPT 27446 to EviCore versus using an older, separately-hosted 'Coverage Policy Number 0347' document (a 2014-dated Cigna policy also covering CPT 27446, found on a third-party site, that I did not verify is still current/live on Cigna's own domain). The patient's appeal letter should therefore explicitly request written confirmation of the exact policy name, number, and version applied to their case, in addition to independently addressing the CMM-311 criteria quoted above, since those are Cigna's current publicly available medical-necessity criteria for this procedure.
